name: webpack-externals-never-needed-when-serverexternalpackages-set
hook: Adding packages to webpackConfig.externals is unnecessary when they are already in serverExternalPackages
body: When a package is listed in Next.js serverExternalPackages, Next.js prevents it from being bundled into client-side JavaScript bundles via its own bundling logic. Adding the same package to webpackConfig.externals is redundant and can cause build failures. The dev branch has no webpackConfig.externals additions and builds fine. The correct approach is: just use serverExternalPackages.
why: webpackConfig.externals and serverExternalPackages serve different purposes — externals prevents webpack from analyzing a package's code, but serverExternalPackages already excludes the package from the client bundle. Adding externals on top of serverExternalPackages can cause webpack resolution issues in edge/server builds.

name: webpack-error-constructor-not-exported-nextjs-15-5-9
hook: minify-webpack-plugin in Next.js 15.5.9 crashes with _webpack.WebpackError is not a constructor
body: The minify-webpack-plugin in Next.js 15.5.9 requires webpack from next/dist/compiled/webpack/webpack and tries to use _webpack.WebpackError to report minification errors. However, WebpackError is not exported from that module. When any minification error occurs, the plugin's error handler crashes, producing '_webpack.WebpackError is not a constructor'. The root cause is the original minification error — the handler crash is a secondary symptom. The fix is to prevent the original minification error from occurring.
why: next/dist/compiled/webpack/webpack only exports { __esModule, default, init } — WebpackError is not accessible. The minify-webpack-plugin's buildError function unconditionally calls new _webpack.WebpackError(...), which fails.

name: ci-fix-attempts-stack-not-replace
hook: CI fixes on this branch were additive — each commit added new webpack config without removing the broken parts
body: The branch 2449-p2-frontend-login-form-silently-fails-session-not has 40+ CI-fix commits, all failing. Each attempt added webpack configuration (externals, .node$ alias, resolve.fallback, etc.) without removing the previous broken configurations. The correct fix was to revert the webpack callback to match dev exactly. Always verify that a CI fix actually produces a passing build before committing it.
why: The webpack callback accumulated multiple conflicting configurations over 40+ commits. Only reverting to the dev baseline (no webpack callback changes) resolved the build.
